newsitem.title: UK: Deaths caused by caterpillars rising in Brazil.
newsitem.headline: Deaths caused by caterpillars rising in Brazil.

text.p: Caterpillars are more deadly than snakes in some parts of Brazil, doctors said on Friday.

In a letter in the Lancet medical journal, Dr Hui Wen Fan of the Hospital Sao Vincente de Paulo in Passo Fundo, Brazil, and his colleagues described the case of a healthy 52-year-old woman who died two days after touching a caterpilllar.

"Considered rare until the 1980s in South America, nowadays envenoming by Lonomia caterpillars is a public health problem in Brazil, particularly in the south where there is an increasing incidence and case-fatality rate three to six times higher than that observed for snake bites," he said.

Fan said the hairs of the Lonomia caterpillar contain a powerful venom that prevents human blood from clotting. Contact with the species causes uncontrolled bleeding after 12 to 24 hours that can lead to death.
He emphasized that quick diagnosis and monitoring for internal bleeding were vital and added that a specific antivenom is undergoing clinical testing.
